text:
alex: quick brain-dump — thinking about a 'micro-bundle' layout for safetensors to speed in-memory hotstart on machines with limited mmap slots. pack many small tensors contiguously with a tiny TOC so we can do one mmap + pointer math, fall back to streaming range requests when mmap unavailable. curious about tradeoffs.
jourdan: interesting. main risk i see is compatibility with our incremental patching + signed/chunked manifests. micro-bundles could obscure provenance unless TOC has chunk checksums.
sarah: +1 on checksums. also how would this interact with prefix cache? if we bundle small embedding layers together, cache evictions might be coarser. could hurt tail latency.
ben: quick sketch i shared in thread earlier — what if each micro-bundle contains small per-layer headers and an optional external index for patching? runtime picks mmap if file descriptor available else streams. fallback should preserve exact byte ranges for verification.
alex: exactly — sketch:
```
MICROBUNDLE V1 header: 16B magic | 8B version | 8B toc_offset
TOC entries: tensor_name_offset | dtype | byte_offset | byte_length | checksum32
payload: contiguous fused tensors (aligned to 64B)
```
alex: runtime flow idea: try zerocopy mmap -> verify TOC checksums -> populate pointer table. if OOM or no mmap -> open range-stream reader that can fetch entries on demand and populate a small mmap-backed slab for hot layers.
jourdan: sounds reasonable. two questions: 1) how to handle partial updates (deltas) w/o rewriting whole bundle? 2) can we interoperate with existing safetensors-only pipelines?
sarah: for deltas maybe support sidecar delta manifests that map into existing bundle offsets (like patch = replace bytes at offset). rewrite avoided for small patches. interop: keep on-disk layout a valid safetensors concatenation? that might be hard.
ben: alternative — keep microbundle as an opaque transport (not strict safetensors on disk) but have an extractor that can emit per-tensor safetensors on demand. pros: you can keep network/storage optimized; cons: tooling needs changes.
jourdan: ops concern: S3 range requests latency spike if we fetch many tiny ranges. need a range-coalescer in the stream reader. batch nearby ranges into one request.
sarah: +1 batch/coalesce. also add prefetch hinting from model metadata: e.g., mark 'embedding layers' hot so loader slabs them at startup.
ben: perf note: single mmap reduces VMAs and syscalls but increases memory pressure when many models loaded. we can use madvise(MADV_DONTNEED) more aggressively on non-hot parts.
warmup-bot: simulated run: microbundle mmap + TOC verify reduces startup syscalls by ~6x, lowers 95p load time by ~18% in our small-model benchmark (on limited-descriptor env).
alex: nice — action items: (1) prototype reader with range-coalescer + slab fallback, (2) define microbundle TOC schema and checksum fields, (3) run patch/sidecar integration feasibility. who volunteers for (1)?
ben: i'll take prototype (1) next sprint.
jourdan: i'll do compatibility explainer for ops and sketch delta sidecar options.
sarah: i'll add perf cases to the warmup benchmark and test madvise heuristics.
alex: awesome. i'll write a short RFC blurb summarizing decisions and tradeoffs. :thumbsup:
